blocks.text: An experimental non-fiction film documenting a weekend spent at the filmmaker's home, captured using nothing but a microphone and a vintage film camera.

The film won Best Micro Short at the BFI Future Film Festival 2024. Besides being screened at BFI Southbank, the film was also selected to screen at the Glasgow Film Theatre and Watershed, Bristol, as part of the festival's first-ever UK-wide programme.
The film has also screened at IndieFlicks and the Sunrise Film Festival, and won a Student Shiny Award.
A horror-flecked psycho-drama that digs into a dark history of hurt, lies, and the traumas of womanhood. Written and directed by Daniella DeVinter, shot in 2022.
Zeb was one of the two cinematographers, and was the lighting designer and sound recorder during production. He was then the primary editor of the film.
An animated film about a student named Little who struggles to fit into their new life at university.
Written by Zeb Goriely and Sophie Stemmons. Animated, directed and edited by Zeb Goriely.
First place at the Film at Jesus competition in Cambridge.

An exploration of masculinity, identity and the relationship between a father and son. Told from the perspective of the son who delivers a compelling recount of the first conversation he ever had with his dad.

Directed and written by Adedamola Laoye. Zeb did the lighting, sound and editing for the film. The film won first place at the Film at Jesus competition, was selected for the Downing Short Film Festival, Oxford University Short Film Festival and Mono Box Short Film Showcase.

Recovering from a mysterious accident, Joss seals himself off from the world, turning to astronomy and living out his life in an observatory. But when he makes an important discovery, his perceptions of reality, and his own past, begin to change into something he can hardly recognise. Convalescence is a voyage into the unknown - whether it be through a telescope or under our very noses.
This was Zeb's first short film, written by Benedict Mulcare, shot in 2019 and completed in 2021.

A documentary about the Duemila30 Lab, a 10-day filmmaking residency that brought 10 social impact filmmakers to Cassine in Italy. The filmmakers were tasked with making short films that engaged with the local community within just 10 days. This documentary about the experience was made within the same 10 days, completed in time for the final screening in the historic Church of San Francesco.
The film was lightly edited the week after to include footage from the final screening, and this version was shown at the Closing Ceremony of the Duemila30 Festival in Milan.

A collaborative film organised by GunPowderHouse, where ten directors each shot one scene of a film, in reverse, only being allowed to see the two scenes that were shot before theirs. Completed over the course of a year, Zeb was the final director to take part, directing the opening scene of the film.

As a freelance filmmaker, Zeb has worked with a wide range of clients, creating launch videos, documentary shorts, and highlight videos. Working primarily as a self-shooter, he offers bespoke film packages which can include motion graphics and hand-drawn visualisations.
For inquiries, contact Zeb at filmbyzeb@gmail.com

blocks.text: Zeb has been posting "content" online since he started his YouTube channel FilmByZeb in 2016. Originally posting simple travel vlogs, he used the channel as a place to document his life, learn filmmaking, and experiment creatively. He has since posted over 100 videos, including several award-winning short films.

Zeb also produces short-form content across multiple platforms. He uses these videos to test creative ideas and methods for storytelling. In 2022, his TikTok on Wordle went viral, reaching over one million views.

His recent short-form series The PhD Grind documented the final year of his PhD using comedy, experimental editing, and animated characters. He is currently in pre-production for a new series about creativity.

Zeb posts his first YouTube video, a simple montage of a family hiking trip. Inspired by Casey Neistat and Sara Dietschy, he edits five vlogs from a later trip to New York. Teaching himself to edit, it takes him seven months to make these five videos.
Zeb begins experimenting with visual editing techniques through short silent videos such as "Rainy Day".
Zeb studied for a Ph.D. in Computer Science at the University of Cambridge from 2021 to 2025. He was supervised by Professor Paula Buttery and funded by the EPSRC Vice-Chancellor Scholarship.

His thesis, titled "Phonological Representations in Language Models", explores the training of small language models with sound-based units (phonemes) instead of text-based units (characters or words). This work draws parallels between modern machine learning methods and statistical learning theories of language acquisition, leading to new insights across both fields.
He was a Research Scientist Intern at Spotify in 2026, studying large-scale entity resolution and LLM-based methods for augmenting labelled data.

blocks.text: Zeb is an award-winning filmmaker with a background in scientific research, having worked on a range of fiction, documentary, and experimental projects.
He was recently awarded the Best Micro Short award at the BFI Future Film Festival for his film 36,000 Words for Love.

In 2024, he was the Festival Director for the 15th edition of Watersprite Film Festival. With a team of 60 students, he delivered a full weekend of free talks, screenings, and ceremonies celebrating the future of film and breaking down the barriers for those pursuing a career in the creative industries.

He recently completed a PhD in Computational Linguistics, exploring whether training AI models with sounds (instead of written language) can teach us something about how children first acquire language.
